title: The Peak Where Learning Becomes the Landscape

features.name: stone path
features.desc-on-touch: Each stone underfoot was placed by a foot before yours. Walking here, you step into a conversation between teachers and the mountain that spans generations.

features.name: ridge marker
features.desc-on-touch: A stone post at the peak, unmarked but worn smooth by hands that stopped here to understand. The understanding was in the view, not the words.

features.name: vista pool
features.desc-on-touch: A mountain pool that reflects not just sky but the teaching-dialogue between each ridge and the air. Drink from here and you know something you cannot name.

features.name: teaching grove
features.desc-on-touch: Wind-twisted eucalyptus at the peak's shoulder, their shapes the landscape's way of teaching silence and persistence without speaking.

features.name: logbook cairn
features.desc-on-touch: A stone cairn holds a weathered book—entries from people who climbed here to learn. Some pages filled with words; others left blank, knowing that silence was the better teaching.

inscription: understanding begins where the ridge and the climber forget which one was teaching the other

file.name: Peak_Climb_Records_1952-1987.txt
file.note: Mountaineering journal entries from multiple decades, clean archive, dated peaks and climbing routes. Margins contain sketches—increasingly, these sketches show the mountain itself learning the shape
